did: Built home's half of the phrase shop. Home now holds the phrase shelf's English intents in its meaning index, and a lookup route answers with the Korean phrases a hunch finds, or says it kept the hunch. A miss is kept in an append-only store in the same request. A spoken hunch is a new kind of voice note, heard in English and never told a phrase, and home looks up every hunch it hears itself, so one the phone stopped waiting for is still kept for the routine that writes phrases. Both pull requests merged.

calls.title: How home gets the phrase shelf's intents (C1605)
options: a synced copy compiled into the server
the build pushes them to home over a route, kept in a table
the phone sends them with every lookup
calls.why: The shelf is the build's, not the owner's data, so it needs no table. Each side copes with the other being ahead: the phone drops ids it doesn't hold, and home names only ids in its copy.
calls.undo: Replace the compiled-in file in file_host::phrases with a pushed store, and delete the copy.

calls.title: The lookup's threshold (C1606)
options: 0.75, with runners-up within 0.1, erring toward a miss
0.6, more paraphrases hit but unrelated sentences sharing words hit too
calls.why: On the real model, unrelated sentences that share an intent's words reach about 0.62 to 0.75, and a miss is kept for the routine while a wrong phrase would be shown to the owner.
calls.undo: Change THRESHOLD and NEAR in file_host::phrases with a new call.

calls.title: How a spoken hunch is heard (C1607)
options: a new voice-note kind the transcriber hears, which can take a minute or more
a route that hears on the request's path
calls.why: Hearing never runs on a request's path, so it reuses the voice-note routes. The take is kept either way, so nothing is lost while it waits.
calls.undo: Drop the hunch kind and roll back its migration, which refuses once a hunch note is held.

left: A check that home's copy of the intents matches some-ui's shelf (server#1262); the shelf reached some-ui main with #3597, so it can be built now.
The phone's adapter and the spoken-hunch port are some-ui's, with KPLAY-LAND (some-ui#3611).
KP5, the routine that reads the kept hunches, is the next story.
